note: cmd/worldedges' rocks for the open edges of a composed world's zones, by the zone's disc file (or FILE#zone): the disc's own art, its records copied into the zone (extras). Chosen and measured off their collision (closed hulls, sides too steep to walk up): foot is the share of a rock's height at which it is widest, where it is set into the ground (a rounded rock set on its bottom leaves gaps under its belly its neighbours do not close); steep the share of its height, from its bottom, a walk does not climb (no face within 48 degrees of flat). Tried and left out: Tunaria's grey dome (0xB8C058DD; its foot is flat and walked up) and grey crag (0x9799723E; its collision is an open shell, 118 open edges up to 83% of its height, so a walk passes through it from behind). steepGround is how much the ground under a rock may rise and fall before the steepest rock is taken (the cone, which grows less than a boulder set to its widest); maxScale the most a rock is grown (a cone 30 times over is a hill). width is a rock's span along the edge (its narrow side, scaled); rise how far its top stands over the highest floor (or water) under it.

rocks.note: a mossy boulder of Odus (zone 10; an LOD of three): widest at 20% of its height, steep to 80%
a dark rock spire of Gerntar Mines (Tunaria zone 143): a cone, steep to 90%
